marta: Quick sync — I want to propose a stricter canary + automatic rollback policy for the new quantized candidate (redwood-llama-3q-v3, int8).
marta: We saw small token-level quality regressions in the A/B but big cost/latency wins. Need an operational rule that avoids serving bad regressions to prod.
priya: Can you paste the A/B summary numbers?
marta: Sure — short summary:
```
A/B (24h, 1M requests):
- traffic split: 10% candidate / 90% baseline
- avg latency p50: baseline 85ms -> candidate 60ms (-29%)
- cost per 1k toks: baseline $0.88 -> candidate $0.62 (-30%)
- EM-like metric (answer-level exact): baseline 0.853 -> candidate 0.846 (-0.7% abs)
- semantic-drift (mean embedding cosine drop): 0.00 -> -0.037
- hallucination-rate (heuristic NER mismatch): baseline 1.2% -> candidate 1.8% (+0.6% abs)
```
priya: Hmm ok. Latency/cost are compelling. But hallucination + EM drop worries me.
kai: What's our decision boundary? We should formalize a compound gating rule: absolute quality delta, relative regression, and semantic-drift windowed check.
ben: Agreed. Propose this rule set (pseudo-YAML):
```yaml
rollout_policy:
  canary_duration: 24h
  initial_traffic: 5%
  ramp: [5%, 20%, 50%] # manual approves between steps
  auto_rollback_conditions:
    - name: absolute_em_drop
      metric: em_score
      threshold: 0.5% # absolute drop
      comparator: '>'
    - name: hallucination_increase
      metric: hallucination_rate
      threshold: 0.4% # absolute increase
      comparator: '>'
    - name: semantic_drift
      metric: embed_cosine_change
      threshold: 0.04 # mean drop
      comparator: '>'
    - name: combined_safety
      condition: 'absolute_em_drop AND (hallucination_increase OR semantic_drift)'
      action: rollback
  hysteresis_windows: 2 # require condition in 2 consecutive windows
  evaluation_window: 15m
```
marta: That matches what I had in mind. Two clarifications:
1) We should prefer absolute thresholds (not relative %) because baseline performance varies across tasks.
2) Hysteresis is critical for noisy short windows.
priya: For semantic_drift, how do we compute it operationally? Embedding system is slightly expensive.
kai: We already sample 5% of requests and compute online embedding difference vs baseline answers. impl detail:
```
SELECT AVG(1 - cosine(a.embed, b.embed)) as mean_drop
FROM sampled_pairs
WHERE time > now() - interval '15 minutes'
```
ben: Also add a lightweight surrogate metric that fires fast: token-level perplexity delta on a small fixed eval set (100 prompts). If perplexity increases > 2% AND any of the other signals then rollback.
marta: Good call. Add `perplexity_delta` as an early-warning metric.
canary-bot: canary scheduled: model=redwood-llama-3q-v3, start=1849002000, initial_traffic=5%
deploy-bot: ran smoke tests: health=ok, kv-cache warmup hit=72% (expected 65-80%).
priya: Operational question — who has permission to manually abort? We need a fast pager path if auto-rollback doesn't trigger but customer-impact observed.
ben: Owner oncall (eng-ml oncall) + product@redwood are allowed. Add a quick `/canary abort <id>` that notifies oncall and product.
kai: Also add an automatic escalation if error-rate > 1% for 5 minutes.
marta: I'll update the rollout YAML in the infra repo and include: metrics emitted, thrift names, and the SQL for semantic_drift.
marta: Next steps: I will open PR with the policy, attach the AB artifact, and schedule the canary start for tomorrow 09:00 PT. If nobody objects by EOD I'll merge.
priya: Please include the fixed eval set and the perplexity surrogate in the PR.
ben: +1 on hysteresis=2, and require two consecutive 15m windows.
kai: +1 — also add a note to ops runbook about manual rollback and how to interpret semantic_drift.
marta: Thanks! I'll post the PR link here once created.
canary-bot: canary started: id=canary-1849002000, model=redwood-llama-3q-v3, traffic=5% at 1849002000
marta: Great — monitoring dash is on `/dash/canary/1849002000`. Watch for `combined_safety` alerts.
priya: I'll set up a quick alert channel `#canary-ops` to get pings.
marta: Ok locking in. If we see >0.5% EM drop + semantic_drift >0.04 across 2 windows then auto rollback.
ben: Also log the decision reason into our canary audit event (so product can see what fired).
marta: Will do. End of thread.
